info.description:
## Protocol compatibility

Base URL: `https://{{API_HOST}}`. Pick a category in the sidebar by use case, then open the matching endpoint. The official models and repository-supported examples in these docs are not the list enabled for your account; the model IDs you can actually use are whatever `GET /v1/models` returns for your account.

```bash
curl https://{{API_HOST}}/v1/models \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $DP_API_KEY"
```

### Choose by use case

| Use case | Recommended entry | Request style |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Chat, reasoning, vision | Chat models | Chat Completions / Responses; Claude and Gemini also have native protocols |
| Image generation and editing | Image models | Images; Gemini image models use `generateContent` |
| Video generation | Video models | Create task → poll status → read the result URL |
| Transcription, translation, speech synthesis | Audio models | Audio; realtime audio uses WebSocket |
| Content moderation | Content safety | Moderations |

One protocol can serve many models, so you don't need a separate interface per model. Chat, image, and video request bodies differ; you can't reuse a request by swapping only `model`.

### SDK Base URL

| Client protocol | Base URL | Main endpoints |
| --- | --- | --- |
| OpenAI-compatible | `https://{{API_HOST}}/v1` | `/chat/completions`, `/responses`, `/images/*`, `/videos` |
| Anthropic | `https://{{API_HOST}}` | `/v1/messages` |
| Gemini | `https://{{API_HOST}}/v1beta` | `/models/{model}:generateContent` |

The Anthropic SDK appends `/v1/messages` itself, so its Base URL omits `/v1`. `/v1/models` returns the OpenAI format by default; with Anthropic or Gemini request headers it can return the corresponding format.

## Chat models

### OpenAI-compatible

- **Endpoints**: `POST /v1/chat/completions` suits traditional chat clients; `POST /v1/responses` suits the Responses API, tool calling, reasoning, and async task plugins.
- **Representative models**: GPT-5.x, GPT-4.1/4o, o3, o4-mini; the recent official catalog also lists `gpt-6-astra`, `gpt-6.1-sol`, and `gpt-6-luna`. These names are catalog information only; check `/v1/models` first to confirm the gateway has them enabled.
- **Dedicated endpoints**: `gpt-realtime-2.1` uses Realtime; `omni-moderation-latest` uses Moderations. Neither accepts chat requests.

### xAI Grok

xAI Grok chat models are called through the OpenAI-compatible endpoints: `/v1/chat/completions` or `/v1/responses`. Whether search variants are available depends on the upstream key and channel configuration.

The recent official catalog lists `grok-4.7`, `grok-4.6`, `grok-4.5`, `grok-4.3`, and the dated `grok-4.20-0309-reasoning` and `grok-4.20-0309-non-reasoning`. For your account, `/v1/models` remains authoritative.

Official docs: [Grok Models](https://docs.x.ai/developers/models), [Responses API](https://docs.x.ai/developers/model-capabilities/text/generate-text).

```bash
curl https://{{API_HOST}}/v1/responses \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $DP_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"grok-4.7","input":"Introduce yourself in one sentence"}'
```

### Claude, Gemini, and other chat models

- **Claude**: `POST /v1/messages`; requests include `anthropic-version`. The official catalog lists Fable 5.1, Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, and Haiku 5.5; older Claude IDs in the repository only indicate existing adapter support, not that the new catalog is enabled. [Official model catalog](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/overview)
- **Gemini/Gemma**: The native endpoint is `POST /v1beta/models/{model}:generateContent`; streaming uses `:streamGenerateContent?alt=sse`. OpenAI Chat/Responses compatible conversion is also available. The official catalog lists Gemini 4 Argon, Gemini 3.8 Flash, and more. [Official model catalog](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/models)
- **Qwen**: Callable via `/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/responses`, and `/v1/messages`, with the extension fields `enable_thinking`, `thinking_budget`, and `enable_search`; also `/v1/embeddings` (`text-embedding-v1`) and `/v1/rerank` (`gte-rerank-v2`). See the "Qwen" endpoint pages.
- **DeepSeek, Kimi, GLM**: Usually go through the OpenAI Chat/Responses compatible endpoints; model mapping may translate the client ID into an upstream ID. Check `/v1/models` and the channel configuration.

## Image models

### GPT Image, DALL·E, and OpenAI Images

- **Text-to-image**: `POST /v1/images/generations`, JSON request body.
- **Image editing**: `POST /v1/images/edits`, `multipart/form-data`; upload `image` and `prompt`, with optional `mask`.
- **Models**:
  - `gpt-image-2`
  - `gpt-image-2.5-flare`
  - `gpt-image-2.5-sunburst`
- Available models are whatever `/v1/models` returns.
- GPT Image usually returns `data[].b64_json`; older compatible models may return URLs. Parameters such as `quality`, `size`, `background`, and `output_format` still depend on the specific model; see the endpoint pages.

Official docs: [Image generation](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/image-generation), [GPT Image 2.5 Flare](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-image-2.5-flare), [GPT Image 2](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-image-2).

### Grok Image, Gemini, and Seedream

- **Grok Image**: The repository's xAI adaptor keeps only `model`, `prompt`, `n`, and `response_format` when converting image requests; it doesn't forward uploaded images, so `/v1/images/edits` is not a verified Grok editing contract. The repository model list is `grok-imagine-image-pro`, `grok-imagine-image`, and `grok-2-image-1212`. New official models are not necessarily enabled on the gateway. [Grok Imagine Image](https://docs.x.ai/developers/models/grok-imagine-image)
- **Seedream**: The `doubao` task plugin declares `openai_image` and accepts requests through `/v1/images/generations` and `/v1/images/edits`; model and field limits vary per model and plugin version. See the Seedream operation pages.
- **Gemini images**: Use `generateContent`; don't rewrite a Gemini request body as an OpenAI Images request body. [Gemini generateContent](https://ai.google.dev/api/generate-content)

### Wan and Qwen image

- **Wan**: `wan2.7-image(-pro)`, `wan2.6-image`, `wan2.6-t2i`, the wan2.5/2.2/2.1 text-to-image models, and `wanx2.1-imageedit` general editing return synchronously through `/v1/images/generations` and `/v1/images/edits`.
- **Qwen-Image**: `qwen-image`, `qwen-image-plus/max`, `qwen-image-2.0/3.0(-pro)`, `qwen-image-edit(-plus/-max)`, and `z-image-turbo`; strong at Chinese and English text rendering and multi-image editing.

## Video models

All video models share two endpoints: `POST /v1/video/generations` submits a task and `GET /v1/video/generations/{task_id}` polls its status; when `data.status` is `SUCCESS`, `data.result_url` is the video URL. Requests accept only the top-level fields `prompt`, `model`, `mode`, `image`, `images`, `size`, `duration`, `seconds`, `input_reference`, and `metadata`; vendor-specific parameters go in `metadata`.

| Family | Representative models | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Wan | `wan3.0-video`, `wan2.7-t2v`, `wan2.7-i2v`, `wan2.6-*`, `wan2.2-kf2v-flash`, `wan2.2-s2v` | `metadata.input` / `metadata.parameters` are merged into the DashScope request |
| HappyHorse | `happyhorse-1.1-t2v`, `-i2v`, `-r2v`, `happyhorse-1.0-video-edit` | The channel must use the custom Alibaba plugin v1.5.1+ |
| Sora | `sora-2`, `sora-2-pro` | `size`, `seconds`, `input_reference` |
| Grok Imagine Video | `grok-imagine-video`, `grok-imagine-video-1.5`, `grok-imagine-video-1.5-lite` | Aspect ratio, last frame, keyframes, and reference assets go in `metadata` |
| Seedance | `doubao-seedance-*` | `metadata` is expanded into the Ark request body |
| Veo | `veo-3.0-generate-001`, `veo-3.1-generate-preview`, etc. | `metadata` becomes the upstream `parameters`; queries return a live simplified structure |
| Kling | `kling-v1`, `kling-v1-6`, `kling-v2-master` | `mode`, `image`, `duration`; last frame via `metadata.image_tail` |
| Jimeng | `jimeng_vgfm_t2v_l20` | `metadata.req_key`, `aspect_ratio`, `frames` |
| Vidu | `viduq2`, `viduq1`, `vidu2.0`, `vidu1.5` | The number of images determines the generation mode |
| MiniMax Hailuo | `MiniMax-H3`, `MiniMax-Hailuo-2.3`, etc. | First and last frames go in `metadata` (H3 can use `images`) |

Official docs: [OpenAI Video](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/video-generation), [xAI Video](https://docs.x.ai/developers/model-capabilities/video/overview).

## Other model endpoints

- **Audio**: `/v1/audio/transcriptions`, `/v1/audio/translations`, `/v1/audio/speech`; Realtime uses the `/v1/realtime` WebSocket.
- **Content safety**: `/v1/moderations`; whether a model is enabled is determined by `/v1/models`.
- **Not implemented**: `/v1/fine-tunes` and `/v1/files` are outside this reference; calling them won't return a valid response.

info.title: Authentication
info.description:
## Authentication

Every endpoint uses the same API key, which starts with `sk-`. The only difference is which request header carries the credential.

### Passing credentials

The gateway accepts `Authorization: Bearer` on every protocol, and on specific paths also accepts each ecosystem's native style.

| Style | Applies to | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Authorization: Bearer <key>` | All | `Authorization: Bearer sk-xxxxxx` |
| `x-api-key: <key>` | `/v1/messages`, `/v1/models` | Default for the Anthropic SDK |
| `x-goog-api-key: <key>` | `/v1beta/models*`, `/v1/models` | Default for the Google GenAI SDK |
| `?key=<key>` query parameter | `/v1beta/models*`, `/v1/models` | Gemini query-parameter style |

Choose one style for the protocol you use; you don't need to send more than one.

```bash
# OpenAI-compatible
curl https://{{API_HOST}}/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $DP_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"your-model","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hello"}]}'

# Anthropic-compatible
curl https://{{API_HOST}}/v1/messages \
  -H "x-api-key: $DP_API_KEY" \
  -H "anthropic-version: 2023-06-01" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"your-model","max_tokens":64,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hello"}]}'

# Gemini-compatible
curl "https://{{API_HOST}}/v1beta/models/your-model:generateContent" \
  -H "x-goog-api-key: $DP_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"contents":[{"parts":[{"text":"hello"}]}]}'
```

### Realtime WebSocket

WebSocket can't set custom headers, so the credential goes in the subprotocol:

```
Sec-WebSocket-Protocol: realtime, openai-insecure-api-key.sk-xxxxxx, openai-beta.realtime-v1
```

### Key permission boundaries

- A key belongs to a **service group**, which determines the models it can call and how usage is billed.
- A key can have a **quota limit** and an **expiration time**; requests are rejected once either is exceeded.
- A key can have an **IP allowlist**. Once set, requests from IPs outside the list return `403`, stating that the IP is not in the token's allowed list.

### Verify your API key

```bash
curl -i https://{{API_HOST}}/v1/models \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $DP_API_KEY"
```

A `200` response whose body contains a `data` array means authentication succeeded. For `401`, see [Error codes](#description/error-codes).

### Authentication FAQ

**Can I put the key in a query parameter for OpenAI endpoints?**
No. `?key=` only works on Gemini paths and `/v1/models`.

**Should I keep the `sk-` prefix in `Authorization`?**
Yes, keep it; the gateway handles it.

**Can the dashboard's Personal Access Token call these endpoints?**
No. Dashboard PATs are for management APIs; model endpoints accept only `sk-` keys.

info.title: Errors
info.description:
## Error codes

### Error response structure

The OpenAI protocol returns an `error` object:

```json
{
  "error": {
    "message": "Error description",
    "type": "new_api_error",
    "param": "",
    "code": "insufficient_user_quota"
  }
}
```

The Anthropic protocol returns:

```json
{
  "type": "error",
  "error": {
    "type": "insufficient_user_quota",
    "message": "Error description"
  }
}
```

`message` is redacted for sensitive information, so raw upstream details may be incomplete. The full error category and status code are available in the error logs in the console.

### HTTP status codes

| Status | Meaning | Action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `400` | Invalid request body, or a parameter is out of range | Fix the request per `message`; retrying won't help |
| `401` | Key is invalid, expired, or disabled | Check the key; create a new one if needed |
| `403` | Egress IP isn't in the key's allowlist, or the account is disabled | Update the IP allowlist or contact an administrator |
| `404` | Path doesn't exist, or the model isn't in the key's group | Check the Base URL and model name |
| `429` | Rate limited | Back off and retry per `Retry-After` or the response body |
| `500` | Internal gateway error | Retryable |
| `502` / `503` | Upstream failure with no available account | Retryable |

### `type` values

| Value | Source |
| --- | --- |
| `new_api_error` | Error produced by the gateway itself |
| `openai_error` | Passed through from an OpenAI-protocol upstream |
| `claude_error` | Passed through from an Anthropic-protocol upstream |
| `gemini_error` | Passed through from a Gemini-protocol upstream |
| `upstream_error` | Upstream returned an unclassifiable error |
| `rerank_error` | Error from the rerank endpoint |
| `midjourney_error` | Error from Midjourney endpoints |

### Common `code` values

When `type` is `new_api_error`, `code` gives the specific reason.

#### Request problems

| `code` | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `invalid_request` | Invalid request |
| `bad_request_body` | Request body can't be parsed |
| `read_request_body_failed` | Failed to read the request body |
| `convert_request_failed` | Request can't be converted to the upstream protocol |
| `model_not_found` | Model doesn't exist or isn't callable |
| `access_denied` | Access denied, e.g. the IP isn't in the allowlist |
| `sensitive_words_detected` | Blocked by the sensitive-word filter |
| `prompt_blocked` | Prompt rejected by the upstream |

#### Quota and billing

| `code` | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `insufficient_user_quota` | Insufficient account quota |
| `pre_consume_token_quota_failed` | Pre-charge failed, usually still insufficient quota |
| `model_price_error` | No usable pricing configuration for this model |
| `count_token_failed` | Token counting failed |

#### Channels and upstreams

| `code` | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `channel:no_available_key` | No upstream account is currently available for this model |
| `channel:invalid_key` | Upstream account credentials are invalid |
| `channel:response_time_exceeded` | Upstream response timed out |
| `channel:model_mapped_error` | Model mapping is misconfigured |
| `get_channel_failed` | Couldn't select an available channel |
| `do_request_failed` | Failed to send the request upstream |
| `bad_response_status_code` | Upstream returned a non-success status code |
| `bad_response` / `bad_response_body` | Upstream response can't be parsed |
| `empty_response` | Upstream returned an empty response |

Errors prefixed with `channel:` come from upstream accounts, not your request. The gateway first switches to the next available account automatically and only returns the error to the caller when no account is available.

### View the full error response

Print the full status code and response body:

```bash
curl -i https://{{API_HOST}}/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $DP_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"does-not-exist","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hello"}]}'
```

A nonexistent model name returns an error body with `model_not_found`, which you can use to confirm your client's error-handling path works.

### Troubleshooting

**Which errors are worth retrying?**
`429` and `5xx`. Other `4xx` statuses indicate a problem with the request itself.

**The information in `message` is truncated.**
Redaction is intentional. Filter the error logs in the console by key, model, status code, and error category to see a more complete classification.

**I keep getting `channel:no_available_key`.**
No upstream account is currently available for this model. Switch to another model or contact an administrator.

post.description:
Wan video generation, covering text-to-video, image-to-video, first/last frame, reference-to-video, and digital human (s2v). The gateway selects the DashScope upstream interface automatically per model.

### Model capabilities

| Model | Resolution (default) | Duration (seconds) | Input |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `wan3.0-video`, `wan3.0-video-prime` | 480P / 720P / 1080P (1080P) | 2–30, `-1` for smart duration | Text, first/last frame, reference image/video/audio |
| `wan2.7-t2v` | 720P / 1080P | 2–15 | Text |
| `wan2.7-i2v` | 720P / 1080P | 2–15 | `media`: `first_frame`, `last_frame`, `driving_audio`, `first_clip` |
| `wan2.6-t2v`, `wan2.6-i2v`, `wan2.6-i2v-flash` | 720P / 1080P | 2–15 | Text / first frame |
| `wan2.6-t2v-us`, `wan2.6-i2v-us` | 720P / 1080P | 5 / 10 / 15 | Text / first frame |
| `wan2.5-t2v-preview`, `wan2.5-i2v-preview` | 480P / 720P / 1080P | 5 / 10 | Text / first frame |
| `wan2.2-t2v-plus`, `wan2.2-i2v-plus` | 480P / 1080P | 5 | Text / first frame |
| `wan2.2-i2v-flash` | 480P / 720P / 1080P (720P) | 5 | First frame |
| `wan2.2-kf2v-flash` | 480P / 720P / 1080P (720P) | 5 | First frame + last frame |
| `wan2.2-s2v` | 480P / 720P (480P) | Determined by audio (<20) | Person image + audio |
| `wanx2.1-t2v-plus`, `wanx2.1-i2v-plus` | 720P | 5 | Text / first frame |
| `wanx2.1-t2v-turbo` | 480P / 720P | 5 | Text |
| `wanx2.1-i2v-turbo` | 480P / 720P | 3 / 4 / 5 | First frame |

- Duration defaults to 5 seconds when omitted; for `wan3.0` smart duration, pass `metadata.parameters.duration: -1` (the top-level `duration` doesn't accept negative values).
- `media` limits for `wan3.0-video`: `first_frame` 1, `last_frame` 1, `reference_image` 10, `reference_video` 5, `reference_audio` 5; first/last frames can't be mixed with reference assets.
- Assets must be publicly accessible URLs.

### Request field rules

The gateway reads only these top-level fields: `prompt`, `model`, `mode`, `image`, `images`, `size`, `duration`, `seconds`, `input_reference`, `metadata`. **Any other top-level field is dropped**; vendor-specific parameters must go in `metadata`, whose structure is described in the `metadata` field below.

- `prompt` is required (pure image-to-video still needs a non-empty prompt).
- `duration` (integer) and `seconds` (string) set the duration, in the range 0–3600; out-of-range values return `invalid_seconds`. Supported durations depend on the model.
- If only `image` is sent, the gateway fills in `images: [image]`.
- `multipart/form-data` is also supported: non-standard form fields are collected into `metadata`, and the `metadata` field can be a JSON string.

### Workflow

1. Submit a task with `POST /v1/video/generations` and save the `task_id` from the response.
2. Poll `GET /v1/video/generations/{task_id}` (every 5–10 seconds recommended) until `data.status` is `SUCCESS` or `FAILURE`.
3. On `SUCCESS`, `data.result_url` is the video URL; upstream URLs usually expire, so download and store the video promptly.

### Error codes

Error responses look like `{"code": "...", "message": "...", "data": null}`.

| HTTP | `code` | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | `invalid_request` | Request body can't be parsed, or `prompt is required` |
| 400 | `invalid_seconds` | `duration` / `seconds` outside 0–3600 |
| 400 | `invalid_multipart_form` | Failed to parse the multipart form |
| 400 | `plugin_request_invalid` | Model parameter validation failed (e.g. unsupported resolution, duration, or asset count); `message` gives the specific reason |
| 400 | `plugin_usage_invalid` | Billing parameters can't be determined |
| 401 / 403 | — | Invalid token, insufficient quota, or no permission to use the model |
| 500 | — | Upstream request failed or server error |
